title: When do children grow the most?
description: Successive ages in the 2019 height columns are compared to find the biggest growth for boys and girls. The trend is then used to estimate heights for ages one to four and for age twelve in twenty twenty nine. Keeko thinks children grow the same amount every year.
teaching_notes: One idea: growth is the later value minus the earlier value, and an estimate should follow the trend you see. Watch for students who spread the growth evenly across the years.

source: Using the 2019 columns, find the largest growth between successive ages for boys and for girls. Then estimate heights for ages 1 to 4, and for age 12 in 2029
video_script.why: The child can read the table of heights and now finds growth between ages and follows a trend to estimate.
video_script.substitution: The book's own table of average heights of boys and girls in India, with the 2019 columns and the 2009 values for age 12.
video_script.anchor: Average heights (cm). 2019 boys: 12: 142.2, 13: 148.4. 2019 girls: 10: 132.8, 11: 138.6. Age 12: 2009 boys 138.9, girls 141.1; 2019 boys 142.2, girls 143.8. Newborn about 50; age 5 about 107.
video_script.wrong_answer: children grow the same amount every year
video_script.wrong_move: Spreads 57 cm of growth equally over 5 years, 11.4 cm a year, and ignores that babies grow fastest in the first years.
video_script.payoff_line: Boys grew most from twelve to thirteen, and girls from ten to eleven.

final_answer.value: Boys grew most from 12 to 13 (6.2 cm), girls from 10 to 11 (5.8 cm); ages 1 to 4 about 75, 87, 95 and 101 cm (estimates); age 12 in 2029 about 145.5 cm for boys and 146.5 cm for girls
final_answer.spoken: boys grew most from twelve to thirteen and girls from ten to eleven; age twelve in twenty twenty nine, about one hundred and forty five point five centimetres for boys and one hundred and forty six point five for girls

maths_rules: boys aged 12 to 13: 148.4 - 142.2 = 6.2 cm, the largest jump for boys
girls aged 10 to 11: 138.6 - 132.8 = 5.8 cm, the largest jump for girls
50 cm at birth to about 107 cm at age 5 is 57 cm, or 57 / 5 = 11.4 cm a year if even
babies grow fastest in the first years, so estimates 75, 87, 95 and 101 cm for ages 1 to 4 fit better than equal steps
for 2029 add the 2009 to 2019 change again: boys aged 12, 142.2 + 3.3 = 145.5 cm; girls aged 12, 143.8 + 2.7 = 146.5 cm
video_script.design: One idea: growth is a difference, and estimates follow the trend. A few table cells sit in the anchor; on the board each growth is a subtraction, the early years are drawn as steps that shrink, and the 2029 values are found by adding the last ten years' change again.
